clue.text: Believes son rolls about in mud

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for son
pigs and buffalo roll about in mud, which is to wallow

explanation.surface: A credulous person is pictured as a son happily rolling about in the mud.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow a story is the idiom for accepting it without question, so it can stand for believes.

clue.text: Begin ignoring Republican in charge still

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so that letter goes

blocks.note: to begin is to start
R is the abbreviation for Republican
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A politician who refuses to deal with a Republican remains in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Static means not moving, the adjectival sense of still.

clue.text: Redesigns plug and fancy taps

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

blocks.note: to plug a product is to advertise it, an ad
the letters of taps rearranged

explanation.surface: A plumber reworks a plug and some ornate taps.
explanation.walkthrough: Plug and taps set a bathroom scene; plug is publicity here.
explanation.definitionFit: To adapt something is to modify it for a new purpose, so it can mean redesign.

clue.text: Slow, large ship

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek myth

explanation.surface: A big vessel moves sluggishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the musical tempo marking for a very slow, broad pace.

clue.text: Swimmer's garment we put on almost finally fit

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, the only letter kept

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of almost
to fit or be right for is to suit

explanation.surface: We manage to squeeze into a swimming costume that nearly fits.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, put on means the first piece sits on top of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A wetsuit is the close-fitting rubber garment worn by divers, surfers and open-water swimmers.

clue.text: A committee on an aeroplane

blocks.note: taken as written
a board is a governing committee, as of a company

explanation.surface: A committee is travelling together on a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers who have boarded a plane are said to be aboard it, a prepositional phrase meaning on the craft.

clue.text: Permit wearing couple's items of jewellery

indicators.note: something wearing a garment is inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a brace is a pair, plus the 's
to permit is to let

explanation.surface: A couple are given permission to wear their jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: Bracelets are ornamental bands worn round the wrist, an example of items of jewellery.

clue.text: Precise account by member of the clergy

blocks.note: AC is the standard abbreviation for account
a curate is an assistant to a parish priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman gives an exact account of events.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means correct in every detail, a synonym for precise.

clue.text: Abandoned pudding disheartened Edward

indicators.note: disheartened read literally means with the heart taken out, so the middle letter is removed

blocks.note: pudding is the British word for dessert
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Poor Edward is downcast after his pudding is left uneaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserted place has been abandoned by everyone, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Answer with unusual clarity, showing eagerness

indicators.note: something unusual is out of its normal form, so the following word is rearranged

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for answer
the letters of clarity rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone replies with surprising lucidity, which shows how keen they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Alacrity means brisk, cheerful readiness to do something, a close synonym for eagerness.

clue.text: North Europeans imbibing cold Tangos, perhaps

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so one word takes the other inside itself

blocks.note: people from Denmark
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Scandinavians are knocking back chilled drinks, or perhaps drinks called tangos.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is also a British fizzy orange drink, which feeds the drinking picture; here it is the ballroom dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is one example of a ballroom dance, so tangos are, by example, dances.

clue.text: The French newspaper's sinister

blocks.note: le is French for the
the FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A French newspaper is described as menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinister is used in its heraldic, Latin sense rather than meaning menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinister is Latin for left, and heraldry still uses it for the left-hand side.

clue.text: Present code Turing almost cracked

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the name is dropped
a code that is cracked is broken apart, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
the codebreaker's name without its last letter

explanation.surface: Alan Turing nearly broke the code before presenting it.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Turing was the British mathematician who helped break the German Enigma code, which makes cracked read as code-breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To present one person to another is to introduce them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Slip from monkey when temperature drops

indicators.note: the abbreviation for temperature drops away, leaving the rest of the word

blocks.note: a monkey is a mischievous child, a little terror

explanation.surface: Someone slips away from a monkey as the weather turns cold.
explanation.walkthrough: Monkey and terror are both affectionate words for a naughty child; T is temperature, removed from the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, so an error is a synonym for it.

clue.text: Area in land with no ice

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: to land a fish is to catch it, as to net it
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A region of terrain is described as having no ice cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Land is a verb here, not the ground under the surface's area.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit served neat comes straight, without ice or a mixer, so the adjective matches.

clue.text: Cautioned about training

indicators.note: about suggests letters moved around into another arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone was warned about their training.
explanation.definitionFit: Education is the process of teaching and learning, a broad synonym for training.

clue.text: A tragedy's opening in that place?

definitions.text: A tragedy's opening in that place?

indicators.note: a word's opening is its first letter, so only that is kept
in sets the first pieces inside the phrase that follows

blocks.note: there means in that place
taken as written
the first letter of tragedy

explanation.surface: Where would a tragedy have its opening night?
explanation.walkthrough: A and T go inside THERE. The whole clue is also the definition, as a play opens in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Plays, tragedies included, open in a theatre, the building where drama is staged.

clue.text: Particular exercises in science fiction chapter

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: sci-fi is the short form of science fiction
PE is physical education, school exercises
C is the abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: A sci-fi novel has a chapter of special training exercises.
explanation.definitionFit: Specific means relating to one distinct thing, a synonym for particular.

clue.text: Likely to change a bra and vile pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are a mess to be reordered

blocks.note: the first letters to rearrange
the rest of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A bra and some horrible pants are bound to be swapped.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants looks like underwear beside bra, but in British slang it also means rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Variable describes something liable to vary, which is to say likely to change.

clue.text: This could give ape food

indicators.note: the answer is read as an instruction whose second half signals a rearrangement of its first

blocks.note: the letters of ape rearranged
the answer split as two words: its second word means crazy, an instruction to rearrange the first

explanation.surface: The clue suggests something you might feed to an ape.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as PEA NUTS, an instruction to scramble PEA, and the result is ape. Peanuts are also a fitting snack for an ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts are a common snack, an example of food.

clue.text: Rock star's initial style

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: the first letter of star
a way of doing something is a style

explanation.surface: A rock star's early musical style.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock is to move to and fro, which is to sway.

clue.text: Job Centre in Exeter's request

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: the middle letter of the seven letters of Exeter's
to request is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone at the Jobcentre in Exeter makes a request.
explanation.walkthrough: A Jobcentre is a UK state employment office; Exeter is a city in Devon. The word Job is the definition, split off from Centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A task is a piece of work to be done, a synonym for a job.

clue.text: University in Turkey prohibits head coverings

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
U is the abbreviation for university
to prohibit is to ban

explanation.surface: A Turkish university forbids certain headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbans are long cloths wound round the head, an example of head coverings.

clue.text: Royal Engineers drink pop

blocks.note: RE is the abbreviation for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Army engineers drink fizzy pop.
explanation.walkthrough: Pop looks like a soft drink beside drink, but it is the noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sharp sound of a gunshot or explosion, a pop.

clue.text: Small diameter frames art gallery announced

indicators.note: a frame surrounds a picture, so these letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the Tate is a group of British art galleries, best known in London
D is the abbreviation for diameter

explanation.surface: A gallery announces it is hanging a small circular frame.
explanation.definitionFit: To state something is to declare it, so stated means announced.

clue.text: Mate's at home drinking tea? On the contrary

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so one word goes inside another
on the contrary flips the stated relation, so the drinker and the drunk swap roles

blocks.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
in means at home

explanation.surface: A friend is at home with a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: On the contrary reverses the stated relation: the tea word drinks in the home word. China is Cockney rhyming slang, china plate for mate.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang china plate rhymes with mate, so china means a friend.

clue.text: American solders in welcome consensus

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for American
to welcome is to greet
read as soldiers: the rank and file, crossword men

explanation.surface: An American is welcoming troops home as everyone agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as published says solders, apparently a slip for soldiers, which are MEN in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A consensus is general accord among a group, which is an agreement.

clue.text: No trouble with student's support for painting

blocks.note: ease is freedom from difficulty
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: An art student's painting stand gives no bother.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the wooden frame that holds a canvas upright while an artist paints.

clue.text: Wonderful, wealthy husband removed make-up

indicators.note: removed means taken away, so the abbreviation for husband is dropped

blocks.note: fab is informal for fabulous
rich means wealthy
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A lovely rich husband has wiped off his cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: Make-up looks like cosmetics but means construction or composition.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabric of something is its basic structure, its make-up, as in the fabric of society.

clue.text: Dad's fun – this might be shown when you go abroad

definitions.text: this might be shown when you go abroad

blocks.note: pa is dad, plus the 's
sport means fun or amusement, as in making sport of

explanation.surface: Dad enjoys himself on holiday overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the travel document shown at border control when entering a foreign country.

clue.text: Washes first of canal banks

indicators.note: first of keeps only the initial letter of the next word

blocks.note: the first letter of canal
an aircraft banks when it leans into a turn

explanation.surface: Someone scrubs the first stretch of a canal's banks.
explanation.walkthrough: Banks looks like a noun for the canal's sides, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash something is to clean it, so washes and cleans are synonyms.

clue.text: Eliot sad mobile's cut off

indicators.note: mobile means moving freely, so these letters move into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A gloomy man called Eliot has had his phone disconnected.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut off as an adjective describes someone separated from others, the sense of isolated.
